steps: Before the bid, Bastelina briefs you on your main rivals: Deepsea Finance, the Imperial Guard, and Omnisky Aegis. You secure the bid, but it also leaves your company staring down a massive funding gap...
13:40, Venatio Month 13th, Silver District in Philae, Soul Shop Corridor
I follow Bastelina up the stairs into an empty hallway.
Bastelina? Am I even supposed to be here? I saw a "Staff Only" sign.
No worries! Boss is adorable Bastelina's VIP. Calling you authorized personnel isn't a stretch at all! ♪
Really? Authorized? That's more than a stretch...
This hallway overlooks the lounge. Following Bastelina's gaze through a hidden window, I have a clear view of those representatives in the lounge.
Since the Desert Scorpions crashed the banquet, you never got to chat with the company reps.
As the Loongs say: Knowing your enemy is half the fight.
Before the bidding starts, let me walk you through their quirks. Hope it helps.
Oh! That'd be incredibly helpful! Thanks, Bastelina!
Alright... Let's start with the most important one over there—
Ugh, nobody here appreciates the beauty of fries. Tragic.
Oh, I know! I'll put the reheated ones in the conference room!==W== Everyone will want a snack when the bidding gets tense. Aren't I thoughtful ♪
Weird, why the sudden chill? Is the AC turned up?
Albedo...?! Uh, heh... Hehe. U-um... I haven't done anything to make you mad today... Right?
Sigh... Honestly, why do you always assume I'm here to scold you?==W== Never mind. I need to run final checks. Come with me to the conference room.
Ah, perfect timing! I was actually about to bring some fries in there for a snack break ♪
In case you didn't know, the Grace Imperium has four parts. Our Soul Shop falls under the Sky Institute.
That was Lady Albedo, Chief Bookkeeper of the Sky Institute, who dragged Laru off. Strictly by the book, she's Laru's superior, and her worst nightmare.
She's overseeing this Monolith bidding. You can count on total fairness.
That armored lady over there is Lady Greyhorn, Knight Commander of the Imperial Guard.
She fights on the front lines, hunting Neo Grace dealers. Her tracking magic always corners her targets—they call her the "Neo Grace Hound."
She values the Guard's image over profit, normally avoiding messy financial events like this.
She's only representing the Imperial Guard at this bidding because she was the closest Knight Commander to Philae. A last-minute fill-in.
Aren't the Imperial Guard a security company? Why would they need a Monolith?
They need steel, and a lot of the steel for their armor only comes from Monolith wishes.
That's the official story, anyway. The truth...==W== Well, I'm crossing a line here. You'll have to dig into that yourself, Boss.
Appreciate it. I'll look into it when the mood strikes.
By the way, Bastelina, one can only participate if they hold a Seal of Grace, meaning everyone here represents a company, right?
Boss Accord meets that bar. But this is a bidding war... What kind of numbers are we talking about?
Setting United Harvest Philae's funds aside, even thinking about Boss Accord's side feels like taking on a century of debt...
This bidding grants ten years of exclusive Monolith access. Going by past averages, a decade's rent easily hits the tens of billions.
Tens of billions...==W== I can already picture the look on Iris's face.
Hehe.==W== I smell it... Oh, I smell it.
Oh? The fries? They do smell appetizing. Let me go grab a plate for you too!
Don't be silly.==W== Not the fries. It's the sweet scent of Dorra.==W== Look at these reps—you can see the greed gleaming in their eyes.
The winning bid will be astronomical. That's when we swoop in and pitch financing to all the poor little ducks desperate for cash.
But what if they play it safe? If the rent stops at around ten billion, they won't really need a loan from us.
If they won't drive up the price, we buy the Monolith ourselves and sublease it. We make a killing either way.
Hehehe, with enough Dorra, you can do whatever you want.
They are Erinis and Meikyo from Deepsea Finance, the top-performing loan officers in the Credit Department last year.
Deepsea Finance is Nova's largest bank, known for fast approvals and fair rates. Boss, if we run short on funds, they might be worth a chat.
The auction will begin shortly. Before it does, take a look at the woman in the corner of the lounge.
That's Mercurio, sole representative for Omnisky Aegis.
They're a massive insurance firm covering all of Nova, and word is that they're sitting on a mountain of cash.
Hmph... Quite the crowd at today's auction.
Number Twenty. Go wrangle a few attendees and pitch our new insurance packages.
They're a newer player with only one Monolith under their belt, but don't underestimate them, Boss. They'll be tough to beat.
Exactly. That's the firm Hazana from the Desert Scorpions was impersonating at the banquet.
They've already put out a statement claiming they were totally in the dark—just another victim of the scam.
The Imperial Guard, Deepsea Finance, and now Omnisky Aegis... This is a crowded field of heavy hitters.
Bastelina, what's the deal with that group over there?
That elegant lady in the kimono? That's Shuo,==W== the manager for Goodwind's Philae branch. She's the real deal.
Goodwind doesn't usually bid on Monoliths though. They're likely just here to maintain their presence and network for new clients.
See those two the Scarlet Sights witch is cornering?
They're Xuan Shi from the territory of Loongs. This event is invite-only, so they must be using "Fenghuang Diner" as a cover.
Hi there! Ophir from Scarlet Sights Media! Got a sec?
Tell us, what's the strategy behind Fenghuang Diner's bid for the Philae Monolith?!
Oh, um, that's a lot... Senior, help! How do I answer this? We're just here for the ride!

Fenghuang Diner is committed to fostering pragmatic cooperation with all representatives through mutual respect. We aim to play a constructive role in Philae's market, driving local growth for the benefit of the community.
We'll share more regarding our bidding strategy and objectives at the appropriate time. No further comments for now.
Uh... Huh? Ah, right...==W== I see. Well, thanks for the insight!
Wow, classic Loong corporate-speak. Total word salad. Did you catch any of that, Boss?
Basically: "We're just tourists with zero interest in the bid, but we can't admit that on the record."
Spot on. Loongs rarely meddle in core affairs outside Cangwu. They're likely just scouting the local market, so they aren't a threat to you.
That's the lineup for today. Bidding's about to start, so let's head into the conference room, Boss.
Right. Still... Something about this feels off.
I know I'm a client, but I'm only renting one safe in your vault. Calling me a "VIP" is a big leap. Why go to all this trouble for me?
Hey, I'm a professional Soul Shop clerk! Helping clients is what I do. Don't worry about it.
Once your company takes off, you'll be renting dozens of safes from us anyway. Consider this an investment in a future big spender!
14:20, Venatio Month 13th, Silver District in Philae, Soul Shop Conference Room
The room is dead quiet, save for the steady rustle of paper as corporate reps pore over the tender documents.
This Monolith bid will wrap up in one or two rounds. Round one is a public auction to set the lease for the next ten years.
The cap is 40 billion, but everyone's looking to slash costs and snag the rights for cheap. Well, mostly everyone. But...
The "auction" is just a label. The final price is likely a given. That's probably why they've got a second round lined up...
Time to make this system work for me.
HQ won't bridge the funds for tomorrow. Can United Harvest Philae handle this alone?
I've checked the data across Nova from the last five years. Winning bids usually fall between 10 and 18 billion.
We've scraped together 20 billion in liquid assets. Based on the trends, we're in the clear.
If we can stay in the game and hit that 18-billion-Dorra mark, we'll force a technical review.
Time's up. We'll open the floor at 4 billion Dorra.
6.6 billion! It's got a nice ring to it.
You're all moving too slowly.==W== 12 billion.
Whoa... 10 billion already? What do you think?
Bastelina was right. Loongs and Goodwind never wanted the bid. They just threw out token numbers before folding.
Deepsea Finance is just driving up the price. This is down to Firenze and the Imperial Guard.
Hmm, no profit margin left at this point. Deepsea Finance is out.==W== Best of luck, you two. Our doors are open if you need a loan.
United Harvest Philae and the Imperial Guard are tied at 18 billion. Any other offers? Hearing none, these two will proceed to the technical review—
Omnisky Aegis?! I thought they were spectating. Why are they jumping in...?
Insane... There's zero profit left. Why is Omnisky Aegis obsessed with this Monolith?
Besides, anything over twenty billion wipes out our liquid assets. What's the plan, Firenze...?
Before I can finish, Firenze squeezes my hand under the table. A silent message: Don't panic. I have this handled.
40 billion? Are you out of your mind?
Heh... Now things are getting interesting.
40 billion.==W== United Harvest Philae, Imperial Guard—your move?
Boss, hehe...==W== Sorry for going rogue here, but...==W== Care to join me in hell? ♪
16:00, Venatio Month 13th, Gold District in Philae, Executive Office
Sorry for the scare back there, Boss.
After the auction, Firenze and I head back to her office.
No need. If the Monolith is essential to United Harvest Philae, it's a necessary expense. Omnisky Aegis and the Imperial Guard were the true wildcards here.
But reality check—how do we cover this 20-billion gap?
We've got three days, right? Has to be in their account by sunset on the 15th?
Yeah. I'll handle it. I made the bid, so I'll find the cash one way or another.
Deepsea Finance is Nova's largest bank, known for fast approvals and fair rates. Boss, if we run short on funds, they might be worth a chat.
Someone from Grace Imperium mentioned Deepsea Finance. Think we could get a loan there?
Excuse me. Lady Firenze, Boss, an invitation just arrived from Omnisky Aegis.
Their rep, Mercurio, is hosting dinner tonight to discuss the auction. They say they aren't looking to monopolize the Monolith.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Seek a loan from Deepsea Finance
If we take a loan from Deepsea Finance or settle with Omnisky Aegis, United Harvest Philae is going to lose its independence.
And if that happens... Firenze, I won't be able to make your wish come true.
You can't get something for nothing. That's just how the world works, right?
Since you said you'd find a way, I'll leave the funding to you.
Grace Imperium's assessment of our wishing ability starts tomorrow—I'll handle that part.
Through thick and thin huh?==W== No problem. I'll scrape up those 20 billion Dorra even if it kills me.
Let's try for a loan from Deepsea Finance.
20 billion... We'll have to give up something big.==W== What are you planning to use as collateral?
How about Boss Accord's Seal of Grace? That should be worth enough to cover it.
But, Boss... That belongs to you.
It belongs to all of us.==W== Besides, this is our best shot at winning the bid and securing United Harvest Philae's future.
If Deepsea Finance lends us that much, they'll be stuck with us whether they like it or not.
Let's take Mercurio up on that dinner and see what she wants.
I'm curious why Omnisky Aegis would pay such a crazy price just for the Monolith's usage rights.
True. What could possibly be worth 20 billion past the break-even point? I'd love to hear her explain that in person.
Yeah. Feels like ... she's after something else.
